overview: Triton is an open-source language and compiler for writing highly efficient GPU kernels using a Python-based DSL embedded in Python (via the @triton.jit decorator). It enables the development of high-performance GPU primitives (e.g. BLAS-level matrix multiplication, softmax, attention) with a block-level programming model instead of per-thread CUDA programming. Triton kernels are compiled through a multi-stage MLIR pipeline: Python AST -> Triton IR (TTIR) -> TritonGPU IR (TTGIR) -> LLVM IR -> target assembly/binary (PTX/cubin for NVIDIA, AMDGCN/HSA for AMD). The core compiler is hardware-agnostic, with backends (NVIDIA, AMD, and out-of-tree/downstream backends such as triton-ascend) plugged in via a Python entry-point registration mechanism and C++ lowering hooks. This commit (040039b88c) corresponds to Triton version 3.8.0 and contains no third_party/ascend directory (that exists only in the triton-ascend fork).

modules.name: Triton Language Frontend (DSL)
modules.description: Defines the Triton programming language as Python APIs: tensor/pointer/dtype types, operators, memory ops (load/store), reductions, scans, atomics, tensor descriptors, and the `semantic` layer that maps Python DSL calls into Triton IR builder calls. Also contains target_info, math, random, and standard modules.

modules.name: Gluon Language Frontend (experimental)
modules.description: An experimental higher-level DSL for explicit-layout programming (warp specialization, TMA, tensor memory, shared-memory descriptors). Gluon kernels compile to TTGIR directly (skipping TTIR), letting users reason about hardware layouts, coalesced encodings, and warp-specialized execution regions.

modules.name: Compiler Pipeline (Python driver)
modules.description: Orchestrates compilation: turns an ASTSource/IRSource into a CompiledKernel by invoking backend-provided stages (add_stages) sequentially, with disk cache lookup, metadata management, IR override/dump hooks, and stage timers. code_generator.py walks the Python AST and emits Triton IR via the semantic layer.

modules.name: Backend Abstraction Layer
modules.description: Defines the BaseBackend (compiler) and DriverBase/GPUDriver (runtime) abstract interfaces plus the GPUTarget dataclass and the entry-point based backend discovery (_discover_backends, _find_concrete_subclasses). This is the primary extension point for new hardware backends such as triton-ascend.

modules.name: Runtime / JIT / Driver Selection
modules.description: Implements the @triton.jit decorator (JITFunction), kernel specialization and caching, argument binding (create_function_from_signature), the global driver selection (DriverConfig via runtime/driver.py), autotuner, async compilation, and the interpreter. The launcher is backend-specific (e.g. CudaLauncher/HIPLauncher).

modules.name: Python Bindings (C++ via pybind11)
modules.description: The `_C.libtriton` module exposing MLIR C++ objects to Python: ir.cc (dialect/builder/ops/types), llvm.cc (LLVM lowering and JIT), passes.cc (pass manager helpers), gluon_ir.cc (GluonOpBuilder), linear_layout.cc, interpreter.cc, and specialize.cc (native_specialize_impl). This is the bridge between the Python compiler and the C++ MLIR implementation.

modules.name: Triton IR Dialect (TTIR) Definition
modules.description: MLIR TableGen (.td) and C++ headers defining the Triton dialect: ops (load/store/dot/reduce/control flow), types (pointer/block types), attributes, traits, and op interfaces. lib/Dialect/Triton/ contains builders, verifiers, canonicalization patterns and transforms (loop unroll, combine, CSE, LICM).

modules.name: TritonGPU Dialect (TTGIR) and Transforms
modules.description: Defines the GPU-level IR with layout attributes (blocked, MMA, shared, distributed encodings), and the vast majority of device-agnostic optimization passes (coalescing, layout conversion removal, software pipelining, warp specialization, dot operand optimization). This is the hardware-layout-aware middle end.

modules.name: Conversion / Lowering (TritonToTritonGPU, TritonGPUToLLVM)
modules.description: Contains TritonToTritonGPU (TTIR->TTGIR conversion) and TritonGPUToLLVM (TTGIR->LLVM, with TargetInfoBase providing target hooks for atomics, barriers, shuffles, TMA, MMA). Subdirs split per op category (DotOpToLLVM, MemoryOpToLLVM, ReduceOpToLLVM, etc.).

modules.name: NVIDIA (CUDA) Backend
modules.description: Complete CUDA backend: Python compiler.py (CUDABackend) and driver.py (CudaDriver/CudaLauncher), C++ TritonNvidiaGPU dialect (TMA, tensor memory, MMA, CLC), NVGPU dialect, and NVGPUToLLVM/TritonNVIDIAGPUToLLVM lowering, plus CUDA language extras (libdevice). Reference implementation of a full backend.

modules.name: AMD (ROCm/HIP) Backend
modules.description: Complete HIP backend: Python compiler.py (AMDGPUBackend) and driver.py (HIPDriver/HIPLauncher), C++ TritonAMDGPU dialect, TritonAMDGPUTransforms, and TritonAMDGPUToLLVM lowering (MFMA/WMMA dot, buffer ops, TDM), plus HIP language extras (libdevice).

modules.name: Proton Profiler
modules.description: A profiling and instrumentation subsystem (hooks, data/context, viewers, proton.py) with C++ support (proton Dialect, TraceDataIO) used for performance analysis of Triton kernels.

modules.name: NVIDIA-specific dialect and instrumentation dialects
modules.description: TritonNvidiaGPU holds NVIDIA-specific IR ops/passes (TMA, tensor memory, mbarrier, warp specialization utilities). TritonInstrument provides sanitizers (FpSan, GSan, ConSan) lowered in lib/Conversion/TritonInstrumentToLLVM.

modules.name: Compiler Analyses
modules.description: Static analysis infrastructure over Triton/TritonGPU IR: alias analysis, allocation analysis, axis/range info, buffer region/index analysis, membar placement, and memory frontier analysis used by optimization passes.

modules.name: Standalone Tools
modules.description: Command-line driver executables: triton-opt (MLIR optimization driver), triton-llvm-opt, triton-reduce (IR reduction for bug reproducers), triton-lsp, and triton-tensor-layout.

modules.name: Tools and Utilities
modules.description: Python utilities: disasm (get_sass), compile, link, gsan, mxfp, tensor_descriptor, ragged_tma, build_extern, and the triton_to_gluon_translator for translating Triton kernels to Gluon.

key_abstractions.name: BaseBackend
key_abstractions.description: Abstract base class for a backend's compiler. It defines how a backend declares target support, converts user options, builds the compilation stage pipeline, loads MLIR dialects, and maps language modules to device-specific implementations.
key_methods: add_stages(self, stages: dict, options: object) -> None (abstract)
get_target_name(self, options) -> str (implicit, used by Gluon)
relationships: Selected by make_backend(target) in python/triton/compiler/compiler.py via supports_target
add_stages feeds the compile() loop which runs stages sequentially
Subclasses: CUDABackend, AMDGPUBackend, and out-of-tree AscendBackend

key_abstractions.name: DriverBase
key_abstractions.description: Abstract base class for a backend's runtime driver. Provides device discovery, target detection, type mapping, and benchmarker selection.
key_methods: allocate_default_profile_scratch(self, size: int, alignment: int, stream)
relationships: Instantiated by DriverConfig in python/triton/runtime/driver.py via _create_driver
Selected through the triton.backends entry-point registry and is_active()

key_abstractions.name: GPUDriver
key_abstractions.description: GPU-specific DriverBase subclass that wires PyTorch device/stream access and profile scratch allocation; most real backends (CudaDriver, HIPDriver, AscendDriver) derive from it.
key_methods: __init__(self) (sets get_device_capability, get_current_stream, get_current_device, set_current_device from torch)

key_abstractions.name: TargetInfoBase
key_abstractions.description: C++ abstract interface providing target-specific code generation hooks during TritonGPU->LLVM lowering (atomics, barriers, shuffles, shared memory, TMA/MMA, printf, assert, address spaces). Each backend implements one concrete TargetInfo.
key_methods: ballot(RewriterBase&, Location, Type, Value) const -> Value
storeDShared(RewriterBase&, Location, Value ptr, Value ctaId, Value val, Value pred) const
loadDShared(RewriterBase&, Location, Value ptr, Value ctaId, Type elemTy, Value pred, Operation*) const -> Value
programId(RewriterBase&, Location, ModuleOp, ProgramIDDim) const -> Value
warpReduce(RewriterBase&, Location, SmallVector<Value>&, ReduceOp, unsigned) const -> bool
assertFail(RewriterBase&, Location, StringRef, StringRef, StringRef, int) const
ascend_implementations: TargetInfo (triton-ascend's concrete TargetInfoBase subclass for NPU)
relationships: Consumed by ConvertTritonGPUOpToLLVMPattern family in lib/Conversion/TritonGPUToLLVM/

key_abstractions.name: JITCallable
key_abstractions.description: Base of the JIT machinery: holds the raw function source, computes a content hash over source + transitively referenced globals/other JIT functions (DependenciesFinder), and enforces global-value consistency across runs.

key_abstractions.name: JITFunction
key_abstractions.description: The object returned by @triton.jit. Implements kernel launch: binds/specializes arguments, computes the cache key, compiles via ASTSource, and launches via CompiledKernel. Uses a per-device binder to reduce launch overhead.
key_methods: __init__(self, fn, version=None, do_not_specialize=None, do_not_specialize_on_alignment=None, debug=None, noinline=None, repr=None, launch_metadata=None)
_do_compile(self, key, signature, device, constexprs, options, attrs, warmup)
relationships: Used by GluonJITFunction (subclass); created by jit() decorator; launches through driver.active.launcher_cls

key_abstractions.name: ASTSource
key_abstractions.description: Wraps a jitted function as a compile source: holds signature, constexprs, attrs, language, and the extension of the first IR stage. Its make_ir() calls ast_to_ttir to produce Triton IR.
key_methods: make_ir(self, target, options, codegen_fns, module_map, context)

key_abstractions.name: CodeGenerator
key_abstractions.description: An ast.NodeVisitor that walks the Python AST of a jitted function and emits Triton/Gluon IR through a semantic layer, performing SSA construction, loop-carried value discovery, and structured control flow (if/scf, while/for) lowering.
key_methods: __init__(self, context, prototype, gscope, function_name, jit_fn, *, options, codegen_fns, module_map, is_gluon, ...)
visit_If(self, node) / visit_While(self, node) / visit_For(self, node)
relationships: Delegates to TritonSemantic or GluonSemantic for op construction; uses ir.builder (pybind)

key_abstractions.name: CompiledKernel
key_abstractions.description: Represents a fully compiled kernel: stores all IR stages (asm dict), metadata (num_warps/shared/target), lazy-loads the binary module/function handles, and exposes run/launch via __getitem__(grid).
relationships: Produced by compile(); consumed by JITFunction.run(); holds backend.binary_ext keyed kernel binary

key_abstractions.name: tensor (and base_value/base_type/dtype/pointer_type/block_type)
key_abstractions.description: The Triton language's value/type hierarchy. base_value/base_type are abstract; dtype/pointer_type/block_type/slice_type are types; tensor/tuple are values; constexpr carries compile-time constants. Tensor operators are defined via _tensor_member_fn and dispatch through the semantic layer.
relationships: Consumed by CodeGenerator/semantic layer; backed by ir.value/ir.type pybind handles

key_abstractions.name: TritonSemantic
key_abstractions.description: The default semantic backend that converts Triton DSL calls into Triton IR builder operations (arithmetic, memory, reduction, dot). Implements the `_semantic` protocol used throughout language/core.py.
relationships: Wraps ir.builder; GluonSemantic is the analogous layer for Gluon

key_abstractions.name: GluonASTSource / GluonJITFunction
key_abstractions.description: Gluon frontend entry points: GluonASTSource sets language=GLUON and ext='ttgir' so the pipeline starts at TTGIR; GluonJITFunction overrides the binder to use GluonASTSource.
key_methods: GluonASTSource.make_ir(self, target, options, codegen_fns, module_map, context)

key_abstractions.name: ir.builder / gluon_ir.GluonOpBuilder
key_abstractions.description: pybind11-wrapped C++ MLIR builders exposed to Python (module `triton._C.libtriton`). The builder creates modules, functions, blocks, and IR operations; GluonOpBuilder is the layout-aware builder for Gluon.
key_methods: ir.builder(context): create_module, get_or_insert_function, create_block, set_insertion_point_*, create_cond_branch, create_if_op, ret, get_int32_attr/get_string_attr
relationships: Underpins CodeGenerator, semantic layer, and backend add_stages implementations

implementation_principles.problem: Turn a Python @jit function into an executable GPU binary with target-specific optimizations while keeping the frontend and core passes reusable across hardware.
implementation_principles.workflow: The pipeline is backend-driven. compile() in python/triton/compiler/compiler.py (1) resolves the backend via make_backend(supports_target), (2) parses options through backend.parse_options, (3) computes a cache key and checks the disk cache, (4) builds a `stages` dict by calling backend.add_stages(stages, options, language), then (5) iterates stages in insertion order (ttir -> ttgir -> llir -> ptx/cubin for NVIDIA; ttir -> ttgir -> llir -> amdgcn -> hsaco for AMD), each stage a function (src, metadata) -> str|bytes. For Gluon, compilation starts at ttgir. Each stage is a pass manager invocation exposed via passes.* from python/src/passes.cc. The final stage returns the binary (cubin/hsaco) for the launcher.
implementation_principles.interactions: compile() <-> backend (stages/options) <-> ir.pass_manager <-> C++ passes <-> cache managers (get_cache_manager/get_override_manager/get_dump_manager). IRSource lets users inject ttir/ttgir/llir/ptx files to override stages for testing.
implementation_principles.platform_differences: The TTIR (make_ttir) and early TTGIR stages are nearly identical across backends; the divergence appears in make_ttgir (architecture-specific passes, e.g. NVIDIA PlanCTA/TMA/warp-spec vs AMD MFMA/buffer-ops/TDM) and in make_llir/make_ptx/make_cubin (TargetInfo + target triple + external assembler). Each backend supplies its own final binary extension (cubin vs hsaco) and metadata packing (pack_metadata).

implementation_principles.problem: Allow multiple hardware backends to coexist and be discovered dynamically, including out-of-tree/downstream backends such as triton-ascend.
implementation_principles.workflow: python/triton/backends/__init__.py defines `_discover_backends()` which reads entry points under the group `triton.backends` (set up in setup.py get_entry_points, one per backend: '{name} = triton.backends.{name}'). For each entry point it imports '{module}.compiler' and '{module}.driver' and calls `_find_concrete_subclasses(module, BaseBackend/DriverBase)` which requires exactly one non-abstract subclass. The result is a `Backend` dataclass (compiler, driver). In-tree backends live under python/triton/backends/ (nvidia/amd symlinked from third_party); external plugins are discovered via the TRITON_PLUGIN_DIRS env var (each plugin dir has backend/name.conf) and registered as `triton.backends.{name}`. `TRITON_BACKENDS_IN_TREE=1` env var provides a fast path that skips entry-point discovery.
implementation_principles.interactions: backends/__init__.py (discovery) <-> setup.py (entry points) <-> compiler.py/make_backend (selection) <-> runtime/driver.py/DriverConfig (driver selection).
implementation_principles.platform_differences: Each backend must provide exactly one concrete BaseBackend and one concrete DriverBase in its compiler.py/driver.py modules; `is_active()` on the driver decides whether a backend is usable on the current machine (e.g. CudaDriver checks libcuda.so presence). triton-ascend registers via third_party/ascend/backend/backend_register.py and a `triton.backends.ascend` entry point.

implementation_principles.problem: Provide a Python-native, block-level programming model and efficiently specialize/recompile kernels for different argument types without per-launch Python overhead.
implementation_principles.workflow: @triton.jit wraps a function into a JITFunction. KernelParam parses each parameter's annotation (constexpr/const/pointer/dtype). On first launch, create_binder() uses create_function_from_signature() to exec a memoized Python function that binds arguments and computes the specialization list (via native_specialize_impl in python/src/specialize.cc). The specialization + options form the cache key; if not cached, ASTSource + CodeGenerator emit TTIR, then compile() runs the backend pipeline. Constexpr arguments are resolved at compile time; do_not_specialize/do_not_specialize_on_alignment control key granularity. DependenciesFinder hashes source + transitively referenced JIT functions/globals to invalidate cache on edits, and re-validates global values at launch.
implementation_principles.platform_differences: Specialization rules are partially backend-driven (BaseBackend.get_int_specialization/get_tensor_specialization/parse_attr) and target-driven (e.g. alignment=16 divisibility attr 'D'). The `Language` enum (TRITON vs GLUON) selects which AST source/stage entry the backend uses.

implementation_principles.problem: Efficiently launch compiled kernels with minimal host-side overhead, including tensor descriptor handling, scratch allocation, and streams.
implementation_principles.workflow: JITFunction.run resolves device/stream via driver.active, retrieves/compiles the CompiledKernel, then calls kernel[grid](*args). CompiledKernel._init_handles() creates the backend launcher (driver.active.launcher_cls(src, metadata)), checks shared memory/tensor-memory/thread limits, and loads the binary via driver.active.utils.load_binary. The launcher (CudaLauncher/HIPLauncher/Ascend launcher) flattens the signature, annotates arguments (constexpr/tuple/kernel), wraps tensor descriptors (wrap_handle_tensordesc), allocates global/profile scratch, and calls the driver's low-level launch function. Forks are handled by not unloading inherited modules.
implementation_principles.interactions: jit.py <-> CompiledKernel <-> driver.active (launcher_cls/utils) <-> backend driver.c / C++ launcher <-> device runtime (CUDA/HIP/NPU).
implementation_principles.platform_differences: Each backend supplies its own launcher class and Utils singleton (load_binary/launch/get_device_properties), C++ type mapping (ty_to_cpp), and tensor descriptor fill (TMA vs backend-specific). GPUDriver handles torch-based device/stream access; non-torch paths use driver.c fallbacks.

implementation_principles.problem: Represent Triton programs in MLIR at multiple abstraction levels, enabling clean separation of target-independent vs target-dependent lowering and reusable optimization passes.
implementation_principles.workflow: Dialects: Triton (TTIR, pointer/tensor ops and control flow), TritonGPU (TTGIR, adds layout attributes describing data distribution across threads), TritonNvidiaGPU/TritonAMDGPU (vendor-specific ops like TMA, tensor memory, MMA), TritonInstrument (sanitizers). Op/type/attr definitions live in include/*/IR/*.td (TableGen) with builders/verifiers/canonicalizers implemented in lib/Dialect/*. Lowering: TritonToTritonGPU converts TTIR->TTGIR (assigning layouts), TritonGPUToLLVM converts TTGIR->LLVM with TargetInfoBase hooks. Transforms in lib/Dialect/*/Transforms run as pass pipelines during make_ttir/make_ttgir.
implementation_principles.interactions: TableGen .td -> generated headers -> lib/Dialect/*/*.cpp (builder/verifier) <-> lib/Conversion/* (patterns) <-> python/src/ir.cc/passes.cc (bindings) <-> Python backend compiler.py (pipeline composition).
implementation_principles.platform_differences: Triton/TritonGPU core dialects are hardware-agnostic; TritonNvidiaGPU (TMA, tmem, mbarrier, MMA) and TritonAMDGPU (MFMA/WMMA, buffer ops, TDM) are vendor-specific. TargetInfoBase isolates per-ISA codegen differences; each backend registers its dialects via load_dialects() and its passes via the `passes.*`/`nvidia.*`/`amd.*` module namespaces.

implementation_principles.problem: Enable a downstream backend (NPU/Ascend) to plug into Triton without forking the core compiler.
implementation_principles.workflow: An external backend: (1) implements BaseBackend (compiler.py) and DriverBase/GPUDriver (driver.py), (2) registers via a `triton.backends` entry point (and TRITON_PLUGIN_DIRS for external source dirs), (3) implements TargetInfoBase and conversion patterns for NPU codegen under its own lib/, (4) optionally extends language (language/ DSL) and costmodel, (5) adds its own stages (add_stages) producing NPU IR/binary. The core pipeline, JIT machinery, caching, and code generator are reused unchanged.
implementation_principles.interactions: AscendBackend.add_stages <-> ir.pass_manager <-> ascend C++ passes; AscendDriver <-> launch <-> NPU runtime; registration via third_party/ascend/backend/backend_register.py.
implementation_principles.platform_differences: Ascend replaces the final lowering stages (LLVM -> NPU IR/binary) and the runtime driver (NPU API instead of CUDA/HIP), while reusing TTIR/TTGIR and the TritonGPU transformation stack. Platform-specific lowering is isolated in third_party/ascend/lib and third_party/ascend/language.

module_dependencies: The layering flows top-down: python/triton/language (DSL) -> python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py (AST->IR) -> python/src/*.cc pybind (ir/llvm/passes/gluon_ir/specialize) -> include/ + lib/Dialect (IR defs + transforms) -> lib/Conversion (lowering) -> third_party/{nvidia,amd,ascend} (vendor dialect + LLVM codegen). Orchestration: python/triton/runtime/jit.py -> python/triton/compiler/compiler.py -> python/triton/backends (BaseBackend/DriverBase) -> per-backend compiler.py/driver.py -> runtime/driver.py DriverConfig. Runtime launch: jit.py -> CompiledKernel -> backend launcher -> backend Utils (driver.c) -> device. Analyses (lib/Analysis) are consumed by Dialect transforms and Conversions. Gluon frontend depends on the same runtime/compiler but starts at TTGIR. Proton (third_party/proton) hooks into knobs.compilation.listener / knobs.runtime for profiling.

hardware_abstraction.description: Triton separates platform-independent abstractions (language frontend, TTIR/TTGIR dialects, core transforms, JIT/caching, compiler orchestration) from platform-specific implementations (vendor dialects, TargetInfo, backend compiler/driver/launcher). The key platform-independent interfaces are BaseBackend, DriverBase/GPUDriver, and TargetInfoBase, plus the shared pass infrastructure in include/triton/Conversion and lib/Conversion/TritonToTritonGPU.
platform_specific: third_party/nvidia/ (CUDABackend, CudaDriver, NVGPU/TritonNvidiaGPU dialects, TMA/tmem/MMA lowering, PTX/cubin)
third_party/amd/ (AMDGPUBackend, HIPDriver, TritonAMDGPU dialect, MFMA/WMMA/buffer-ops/TDM lowering, AMDGCN/hsaco)
third_party/ascend/ (in triton-ascend fork; AscendBackend, AscendDriver, NPU lowering)

interface_surface.description: The set of interfaces that an external hardware backend (triton-ascend) must implement or subclass to integrate with Triton. These are the load-bearing seams for ascend_impact analysis: signature/behavior changes to any of them will affect triton-ascend.

key_methods: add_stages(self, stages: dict, options: object) -> None (abstract)
inheritable_interfaces.impact_rule: Any signature change to the abstract methods (add/remove/rename parameter, change return type, or add a new abstractmethod) breaks AscendBackend and all backends. Changes to add_stages stage keys/order or the stage callable signature (src, metadata) affect the compile loop. Adding a new abstractmethod makes AscendBackend abstract (fails _find_concrete_subclasses). Changing parse_options/pack_metadata contracts affects metadata and launcher ABI.

key_methods: allocate_default_profile_scratch(self, size: int, alignment: int, stream)
inheritable_interfaces.impact_rule: Adding/removing abstract methods or changing is_active() selection semantics affects backend discovery (runtime/driver.py _create_driver). get_current_target must return a GPUTarget matching the backend's supports_target. Changes here break all concrete drivers including AscendDriver.

Attributes `utils` (backend Utils singleton) and `launcher_cls` are consumed by CompiledKernel._init_handles and JITFunction.run. Removing/renaming these or changing the launcher __call__ signature (gridX, gridY, gridZ, stream, function, kernel_metadata, launch_metadata, launch_enter_hook, launch_exit_hook, *args) breaks AscendDriver's launcher.

key_methods: ballot(RewriterBase&, Location, Type, Value) const -> Value
storeDShared(RewriterBase&, Location, Value, Value, Value, Value) const
loadDShared(RewriterBase&, Location, Value, Value, Type, Value, Operation*) const -> Value
programId(RewriterBase&, Location, ModuleOp, ProgramIDDim) const -> Value
warpReduce(RewriterBase&, Location, SmallVector<Value>&, ReduceOp, unsigned) const -> bool
assertFail(RewriterBase&, Location, StringRef, StringRef, StringRef, int) const
inheritable_interfaces.impact_rule: Any change to a pure-virtual method signature requires recompilation of Ascend's TargetInfo and will fail to link if not updated. Adding a new pure-virtual method forces Ascend to implement it (compile error). Changing shared-memory address-space mapping, atomics scope, or barrier semantics changes generated code for all backends.

inheritable_interfaces.ascend_impl: Reused unchanged (no Ascend-specific override; Gluon uses GluonJITFunction)
key_methods: JITFunction._pack_args(self, backend, kwargs, bound_args, specialization, options)
inheritable_interfaces.impact_rule: Ascend does not subclass these, but relies on their behavior. Changes to specialization key format, cache key computation, or binder output shape affect Ascend kernels identically to all backends (no ascend-specific guard needed, but any change here is transitively impactful).

inheritable_interfaces.ascend_impl: Reused unchanged (Gluon subclasses it; Ascend reuses the Triton ASTSource)
key_methods: make_ir(self, target, options, codegen_fns, module_map, context)
inheritable_interfaces.impact_rule: The make_ir contract (returns an MLIR module consumed by the first pipeline stage) and hash() are core to the compile loop. Ascend reuses these as-is; changes affect all backends.

not_used_by_ascend: third_party/nvidia/** (CUDABackend, CudaDriver, CudaLauncher, NVGPU/TritonNvidiaGPU dialects, TritonNVIDIAGPUToLLVM lowering, PTX/cubin stages)
third_party/amd/** (AMDGPUBackend, HIPDriver, HIPLauncher, TritonAMDGPU dialect/lowering, AMDGCN/hsaco stages)
third_party/proton/** (unless Ascend explicitly opts into Proton)
python/triton/language/extra/libdevice** (NVIDIA libdevice path mapping, but get_module_map is backend-driven)
lib/Conversion/TritonGPUToLLVM/** (NVIDIA/AMD TargetInfo and PTX/AMDGCN-specific patterns, unless Ascend reuses the base patterns)
bin/ triton-llvm-opt.cpp, triton-reduce.cpp (NVIDIA-targeted tooling, though triton-opt/triton-reduce are dialect-generic)
test/** and python/test/unit/cuda/** (NVIDIA-only tests) and python/test/backend/test_device_backend.py mirrors
tutorials/ and python/tutorials/ (NVIDIA-oriented examples; not part of the compiled backend)
python/triton/runtime/build.py compile_module_from_file paths tied to CUDA/HIP include/lib dirs
python/triton/compiler/make_launcher.py (empty/stub; the real launcher is per-backend in driver.py)

test_structure.path: python/test/ (pytest), test/ (lit, MLIR-level), unittest/ (C++ gtest), third_party/{amd,nvidia}/unittest/ and third_party/{amd,nvidia}/python/test/
test_structure.description: Testing is layered: python/test/unit/ contains GPU pytest tests (language/, runtime/, cuda/); python/test/backend/ and python/test/gluon/ cover backends and Gluon; test/ holds lit tests for MLIR pass/IR transformations (Analysis, Conversion, Triton, TritonGPU, TritonNvidiaGPU, Gluon, Hopper); unittest/ holds C++ gtest for Analysis/Dialect/Tools (e.g. LinearLayout, LayoutUtils, Dialect tests). lit tests run via `cd BUILD_DIR; ninja triton-opt; lit -v test/<path>.mlir`; pytest uses `-s --tb=short`; single tests via `pytest file.py::test_name`. triton_kernels/tests/ holds numerical/performance kernel tests.

patch_catalog.note: This is the upstream triton-lang/triton repository (commit 040039b88c). There is no third_party/ascend/patch/ directory here; the patch catalog is populated only when analyzing the triton-ascend fork. llvm_patch_*.patch and triton-ascend-dev-*.patch are intentionally excluded per the analysis scope.

steps: 在 python/triton/language/ 中定义 Python API（语义约定 + 类型签名）
在 include/ 中声明 IR op，在 lib/Dialect/Triton*/ 中实现（builder、verifier、canonicalization）
必要时在 python/src/ 和 lib/Conversion/ 中添加 lowering pass
添加 lit 测试：test/ 下对应目录

definitely_affected_paths.reason: BaseBackend 抽象方法（supports_target/hash/parse_options/add_stages/load_dialects/get_module_map）签名增删或 GPUTarget 字段变更会直接破坏 AscendBackend 的实例化与 compile() 调用；add_stages 阶段键/顺序与阶段回调 (src, metadata) 约定是 Ascend 多阶段编译链的核心。
DriverBase 抽象方法（is_active/map_python_to_cpp_type/get_current_target/get_active_torch_device/get_benchmarker）增删或签名变更会破坏 NPUDriver 与 _create_driver 的选择逻辑；is_active 语义变化会直接导致 Ascend 后端无法激活。
后端发现机制（_discover_backends/_find_concrete_subclasses、entry_points group='triton.backends'、TRITON_BACKENDS_IN_TREE 快路径）是外部插件后端的唯一接入入口，逻辑变更会破坏 Ascend 的注册与发现。
TritonSemantic.dot 被 _patched_dot monkey-patch 覆写，dot 签名/默认值变化会使 patch 调用 TypeError；tf32→hf32 与 max_num_imprecise_acc=None 拦截逻辑依赖上游 dot 实现细节。
CodeGenerator.__init__ 被 _patched_cg_init monkey-patch 注入 hacc.target，__init__ 参数或 module.set_attr 时机变更会导致 patch 失效；该 patch 依赖 self.builder.options.arch 与 ascendnpu_ir_builder 可用。
模块级 parse 被 _patched_parse 覆写扩展 ttir/ttgir/npubin/mlirbc 分支；同时 ASTSource/compile() 主流程与 add_stages 阶段循环被 Ascend 直接复用，扩展名集合/返回类型约定变更会使 ir_override 与 TRITON_KERNEL_OVERRIDE 失效。
TritonOpBuilder 构造器签名或基础 builder 接口（getI64ArrayAttr 等）变更会影响 AscendNPUIROpBuilder 的继承与 ascendnpu_ir_builder 绑定，导致 Ascend 扩展 op 构造失败。
InterpreterBuilder 的 op 解释执行注册协议及 ReduceOps/ScanOps 基类接口变更需 AscendInterpreterBuilder/AscendReduceOps/AscendScanOps 同步，否则 CPU 解释执行 Ascend kernel 失败。
AutoTilingTuner 继承 Autotuner，Autotuner 的 __init__/run/benchmark 签名或调优协议变更会影响 Ascend 的 tiling/num_stages/multibuffer 参数展开。
JITFunction/JITCallable 被 Ascend 直接复用，特化键、缓存键计算与参数绑定格式变更会影响 Ascend kernel 的编译缓存与启动器生成。
tt 方言 op/类型/属性定义是 TTIR 的唯一来源，Ascend 复用 AST→TTIR 前端并从此处开始 TritonToLinalg 转换，任何 op 定义/verifier/属性变更都会改变 Ascend lowering 的输入。
tt 方言 builder/verifier/canonicalization 与 transforms（loop unroll/combine/CSE/LICM）变更影响 TTIR 语义，进而影响 Ascend 的 TritonToLinalg 转换链。

potentially_affected_paths.reason: 前端类型系统（tensor/dtype/pointer_type/constexpr）与算子语义（类型检查/常量折叠）行为变更会影响所有后端生成的 AST/TTIR；仅在涉及 Ascend 实际使用的算子或改变 IR 输出形态时才会传导到 Ascend。
编译流水线框架（CompiledKernel、元数据缓存、stage 间通信、make_ir 契约）变更可能影响 Ascend 的多阶段编译，但若 Ascend 通过 add_stages 自提供大部分阶段则影响有限。
_create_driver 全局驱动选择、DriverConfig 与缓存逻辑变更可能影响 NPUDriver 的激活与设备选择，视与 Ascend 驱动的耦合程度而定。
编译产物磁盘缓存与 code_cache 键格式变更可能影响 Ascend kernel 的缓存命中，但属于通用路径影响。
Ascend 不走 TTGIR（用 TritonToLinalg 替代），但若复用共享 MLIR 基础设施/类型或 Python 前端间接引用 ttg 类型，相关变更可能间接影响 Ascend。
TritonGPU 优化 pass 与 layout 一般不影响 Ascend，但共享的 MLIR 类型定义或 Analysis 基础设施变更可能间接传导。
别名/分配/AxisInfo/Membar 等分析若被 Ascend 的 pass 复用则变更会传导，否则无影响。
同上，静态分析实现变更仅在 Ascend 复用对应分析时影响。
pass manager 绑定接口变更可能影响 Ascend 通过 _C 驱动自定义 pass 的方式。
triton-opt 是方言通用工具，Ascend 若依赖其加载自定义方言/pass 则变更可能影响其 lit 测试与调试流程。
Gluon 编译到 TTGIR，Ascend 默认不使用；但若上游将 Gluon 能力下沉并改变 ASTSource/JITFunction 基类行为，则可能间接传导到 Ascend。

never_affected_paths.reason: CUDA 后端（CUDABackend/CudaDriver/CudaLauncher/PTX 生成/TritonNvidiaGPU）纯 NVIDIA 专属，Ascend 不修改也不依赖，仅作为共存参照。
AMD/HIP 后端（HIPBackend/HIPDriver/GCN 生成/TritonAMDGPU）纯 ROCm 专属，与 Ascend 无耦合。
独立 f2reduce 工具，Ascend 不使用。
性能剖析框架独立于后端，除非 Ascend 显式启用否则无影响。
CUDA 专属 libdevice 与语言扩展，Ascend 使用 third_party/ascend/language/cann/libdevice.py。
NVIDIA libdevice 路径映射由后端 get_module_map 驱动，Ascend 用 CANN libdevice 替代。
NVIDIA 专属方言（TMA/tensor memory/mbarrier/warp specialization），Ascend 不加载。
AMD 专属方言，Ascend 不加载。
TritonGPU→LLVM lowering 仅 NVIDIA/AMD 使用，Ascend 用 TritonToLinalg 替代，此路径完全跳过。
TargetInfoBase 是 NV/AMD TargetInfo 的硬件抽象，Ascend 无实现也不调用，纯虚方法增删不影响 Ascend 编译链。
Gluon NVIDIA 后端专属实现。
Gluon AMD 后端专属实现。
CUDA 专属测试，不影响 Ascend 构建与运行。
NVIDIA 导向示例，不参与后端编译。
